items.title: Fable 5.1 Solves the Cyphral Distich, a 370-year-old cipher
items.author: u1hcw9nx
items.summary: In 2026, an AI named Claude Fable 5.1 solved a 370-year-old cipher known as the Cyphral Distich in forty-four minutes. The cipher was originally created by Sir Thomas Urquhart. The solution revealed hidden text praising a royal figure.

items.author: simonpure
items.summary: Open-source AI includes notable models like Open Assistant, BLOOM, and OPT, fostering innovation and collaboration. Key resources include the Xfinit Software reading list and Interconnects' open-source AI articles. Wikipedia lists various open-source AI software tools.

items.title: Show HN: Is It Greg?
items.author: antoineleclair
items.text:
My friend Greg often posts incredible things he just made, just for fun.

Often, I don't realize that it's something HE made and then I see the URL, AND IT'S MY FRIEND, GREG!

A few things he made that I think are amazing:

- ikea complexity index: https://ikea.greg.technology/

- Boing: https://boing.greg.tec
items.summary: "Is It Greg?" is a Show HN submission on Hacker News where users can play with a project. Show HN requires a working product for public interaction. Submissions must follow guidelines to avoid misuse.

items.title: AI is not a normal technology
items.author: theahura
items.summary: AI is not a normal technology due to its unique capabilities and potential for transformative impacts on society, economy, and governance. It differs from typical technologies by its autonomous and creative problem-solving abilities.

items.title: Making Startups Powerful
items.author: tosh
items.summary: Successful startups focus on strong products, effective go-to-market strategies, and strong organizational cultures. Effective teams and clear objectives are also crucial. Network effects and scalable models enhance startup power.

items.title: I build a mechanical watch face: a real gear train for a watch with no gears
items.author: tomasslavicek
items.summary: To build a mechanical watch face without gears, use alternative components like ruby jewels for low friction. Watchmaking kits are available for DIY enthusiasts. Mechanical watch movements rely on intricate gear trains for timekeeping.

items.title: "Chilling" warning or overreaction? AI bioweapons report divides experts
items.author: sbulaev
items.summary: Experts are divided on whether AI bioweapons reports are a chilling warning or an overreaction, with some fearing AI could develop dangerous biological weapons, while others believe the risk is overstated. The debate centers on AI's potential to cause havoc, including through bioweapons. The urgency of the issue remains a topic of significant discussion.

items.title: Reverse-Engineering Claude Web's MicroVM: Uncovering Anthropic's Hidden Antspace
items.author: rzk
items.summary: Anthropic developed a hidden PaaS platform called "Antspace" within their microVM for deploying applications, rivaling Vercel and others. It powers their web app builder on claude.ai. Antspace integrates the entire stack from models to hosting.

items.title: AI Robots – When will they be in our homes
items.author: andsoitis
items.summary: Humanoid robots are expected to enter homes in 3-7 years. Some companies are already testing robots in homes. The timeline may vary based on technological advancements and challenges.

items.title: Sean Carroll explains the biggest ideas in the universe – Full Interview [video] (2025)
items.author: binyu
items.summary: Sean Carroll discusses major concepts in the universe in a 2025 interview and a 2026 book titled "The Biggest Ideas in the Universe." He is a professor at Johns Hopkins University and an expert in cosmology and gravitation.

items.title: Garry Tan wants US open-weight AI labs to 'distill' frontier models, too
items.author: TheJCDenton
items.summary: Garry Tan advocates for U.S. open-weight AI labs to use distillation techniques on frontier models to enhance access and competition. He believes this approach can democratize AI and reduce reliance on Chinese models. This strategy aims to balance innovation with public access.

items.title: David Sacks: OpenAI and Anthropic Don't Need Regulations to Pace Frontier Models
items.author: kolanos
items.summary: David Sacks argues that leading AI companies like Anthropic and OpenAI don't need regulatory approval to slow down their models, as they have the control and resources to manage risks themselves. He believes self-regulation is sufficient for safety. He also stated they should stop seeking legal cover from Washington.

items.title: Mark Zuckerberg: "Cambridge Analytica" (2017)
items.author: mfiguiere
items.summary: In 2017, Mark Zuckerberg considered naming Cambridge Analytica alongside Russian actors in an election security assessment but ultimately did not. In 2018, Zuckerberg testified before Congress about the scandal and Facebook's response. Facebook was fined $5 billion in 2019 for privacy violations related to the data scandal.

items.title: Device Drivers lab exercise – COSC562
items.author: azhenley
items.summary: COSC562 is a lab exercise focused on device drivers, utilizing Rust for development. The course covers topics like PCI and Rust programming. The lab emphasizes writing device drivers in Rust.

items.title: TailTalk: A modern async user space AppleTalk stack with Rust and Tokio
items.author: zdw
items.summary: TailTalk is a Rust-based async user space AppleTalk stack. It supports multiple AppleTalk protocols and runs on Linux, Mac OS, and Windows. It uses Tokio for asynchronous operations.

items.title: Navier-Stokes Visualized as 1kB i386 demos
items.author: chaostaco
items.summary: The Navier-Stokes equations describe fluid flow, and a 1kB i386 demo visualized the solution to this problem using AI. The demo shows fluid dynamics, crucial for simulations in engineering and video games. The visualization is based on a custom Three.js/WebGL renderer.
